# Prowlarr

Prowlarr manages your indexers in one place and syncs them to Sonarr and Radarr.
Mediaplane runs the upstream LinuxServer.io image, unmodified. Prowlarr gets no data
folder, only its own config folder.

<!-- BEGIN GENERATED by "pnpm docs:generate" from app.ts. Do not edit. -->

## What Mediaplane sets

- **Image:** `lscr.io/linuxserver/prowlarr:2.6.5.5623-ls163`
- **Digest:** `sha256:f9151e5bc1025c6d0a630d503210cdcb6bb55a7cc098562609d96a408d838902`
- **Architectures:** amd64, arm64
- **Ports:** 9696/tcp (web), published as `network.bind` says; `apps.prowlarr.port` moves the host port
- **Volumes:** `<home>/appdata/prowlarr` → `/config`
- **Runs as:** the stack's `user:`, through `PUID` and `PGID`
- **Health check:** `curl -fsS http://localhost:9696/ping`, every 30s (timeout 10s, 5 retries, 60s to start)
- **Secrets:** `apiKey`: 32 random hex characters, generated once and kept in `state/secrets.json`
- **API:** on its `web` port, which Mediaplane reaches over the stack's wiring network, with `apiKey` in the `X-Api-Key` header
- **Managed in the app:** `prowlarr.admin`: fields `prowlarr.admin.username` (fixed); the secret `password`, checked and never shown. `prowlarr.application_sonarr`: fields `prowlarr.application_sonarr.prowlarrUrl` (fixed), `prowlarr.application_sonarr.baseUrl` (fixed), `prowlarr.application_sonarr.syncLevel`, `prowlarr.application_sonarr.syncCategories`; the secret `apiKey`, checked and never shown. `prowlarr.application_radarr`: fields `prowlarr.application_radarr.prowlarrUrl` (fixed), `prowlarr.application_radarr.baseUrl` (fixed), `prowlarr.application_radarr.syncLevel`, `prowlarr.application_radarr.syncCategories`; the secret `apiKey`, checked and never shown. `prowlarr.indexer_proxy`: fields `prowlarr.indexer_proxy.host` (fixed), `prowlarr.indexer_proxy.requestTimeout`, `prowlarr.indexer_proxy.tags`
- **Needs:** nothing
- **Provides:** `indexer-manager`
- **Also turns on:** `byparr`, with the default settings

## What Mediaplane does today

- **Its API key.** Generated once, and passed in `PROWLARR__AUTH__APIKEY`.
- **`config.xml`, before its first start.** Mediaplane writes
  `appdata/prowlarr/config.xml` with the API key and the login settings below, only if the
  file doesn't exist. Prowlarr keeps them and adds the rest of its settings, so it keeps
  its key even if the variable is ever lost. Mediaplane never changes the file after
  that.
- **Its login.** `PROWLARR__AUTH__METHOD` is `Forms`. `PROWLARR__AUTH__REQUIRED` is
  `Enabled`, or `DisabledForLocalAddresses` when `security.login_on_lan` is `false`. In
  that case, while the web UI is published on your LAN (`network.bind` `lan` or `all`),
  `PROWLARR__SERVER__TRUSTEDNETWORKS` lists your LAN subnet, when Mediaplane knows it.
- **The shared admin login.** Once Prowlarr runs, `apply` sets the login that
  `mediaplane credentials` shows, through Prowlarr's API, and checks it by signing in. It
  is the resource `prowlarr.admin`: its user name is managed, and its password is a secret,
  which `state/resources.json` names but never holds. Prowlarr needs no restart for
  it. Mediaplane reaches Prowlarr's API over the stack's wiring network, with its API key.
- **The names a browser may use, without a login on the LAN.** With
  `security.login_on_lan: false`, Prowlarr takes only the Host names in
  `PROWLARR__SERVER__ALLOWEDHOSTS`, and refuses to save its settings without them:
  Mediaplane lists `prowlarr`, which the other apps and Mediaplane use, and the addresses its
  web UI is published on. `localhost` and `127.0.0.1` always work. To use another name,
  such as your host's, set the variable yourself in `apps.prowlarr.env`, keeping `prowlarr` in
  the list, with commas between the names.
- **Its links to Sonarr and Radarr** (`prowlarr.application_sonarr` and
  `prowlarr.application_radarr`). For each of them in the stack, `apply` adds an
  application to Prowlarr, `Sonarr (Mediaplane)` or `Radarr (Mediaplane)`, with full
  sync, so that the indexers you add in Prowlarr reach the arr:
  - Prowlarr reaches the arr as `http://sonarr:8989` or `http://radarr:7878`, and the arr
    reaches Prowlarr back as `http://prowlarr:9696`, on the stack's network;
  - it syncs Prowlarr's own default categories for that app:
    - to Sonarr: 5000, 5010, 5020, 5030, 5040, 5045, 5050 and 5090, which is TV without
      5060 and 5080 (sport and documentary). Sonarr's anime categories, 5070, stay as
      Prowlarr set them, and are yours;
    - to Radarr: 2000, 2010, 2020, 2030, 2040, 2045, 2050, 2060, 2070, 2080 and 2090, which
      is all of Movies;
  - its key is the arr's, which Prowlarr shows masked. `plan` and `apply` check it with
    Prowlarr's own test of the link, which calls the arr with the key and has the arr
    call Prowlarr back: a refused key is set again, and any other failure is Prowlarr's
    own message. While the arr isn't up, or its admin login is yet to be set, `plan`
    leaves that check to `apply`;
  - its other settings, such as its tags, are yours: `apply` leaves them as they are.
- **The indexer proxy** (`prowlarr.indexer_proxy`). `apply` adds the stack's Cloudflare
  solver to Prowlarr as an indexer proxy, `Cloudflare (Mediaplane)`, of type FlareSolverr,
  which Byparr answers too: `http://byparr:8191/`, or `http://flaresolverr:8191/` when you
  list FlareSolverr, with a 60-second timeout and the tag `cloudflare`, which `apply`
  makes in Prowlarr when it isn't there.
- **Byparr.** Listing Prowlarr also turns on Byparr, the Cloudflare challenge solver,
  unless you list FlareSolverr instead or set `byparr: { enabled: false }`. Without a
  solver, Mediaplane adds no indexer proxy.
- **Its web UI,** published as `network.bind` says. `mediaplane credentials` shows its
  address.

## What stays yours

Mediaplane never adds indexers. You add them once in Prowlarr, and it syncs them to Sonarr
and Radarr, where they show as `<name> (Prowlarr)`. Change them in Prowlarr, not in the
arrs: Prowlarr puts its own settings back.

To send an indexer through the Cloudflare solver, give it the tag `cloudflare` in
Prowlarr (Indexers, then edit the indexer, then Tags). Prowlarr sends an indexer through a
proxy only when they share a tag. Even then it asks the indexer itself first, and turns
to the solver only when the site answers with a Cloudflare challenge.

## Drift and Keep mine

- **What drift reports.** `mediaplane drift`, and `plan`, report a change made in
  Prowlarr's web UI to what Mediaplane manages here, listed above under "Managed in the
  app": what Mediaplane set, and what Prowlarr holds now. A secret is checked with
  Prowlarr's own test, and named, never shown. `apply` puts each back.
- **Keeping yours.** `mediaplane keep prowlarr.<resource>.<field>`, as drift names it,
  keeps what Prowlarr holds instead: it adds the line under `overrides:` in `stack.yaml`,
  and `apply` then leaves it. A field marked `(fixed)` above, and a secret, can't be
  kept. `mediaplane keep prowlarr.indexer_proxy` stops Mediaplane managing a resource deleted
  in Prowlarr. The [drift runbook](../../docs/runbooks/drift-reported.md) says more.
- **Where Prowlarr sends a key** is fixed: each link's `baseUrl` and `prowlarrUrl`, and
  the proxy's host, which your indexers' requests go through. Drift reports a change to
  one, and `apply` puts the stack's own address back; Prowlarr's test of a link is
  always aimed there.
- **A link's categories,** kept (`prowlarr.application_sonarr.syncCategories`): each is
  a number, such as `5000`, separated by `,`. `keep` and `plan` refuse one that isn't.
- **The proxy's tags,** kept with other labels than `cloudflare`
  (`prowlarr.indexer_proxy.tags`): Mediaplane gives the proxy each, making a tag it
  lacks.
- **The proxy's health.** Mediaplane never tests the proxy itself, which needs the
  internet: drift reads Prowlarr's own health check, which tests it every six hours, and
  warns (`drift.health`) when it says the proxy is unavailable. `apply` can't put that
  right: check the Cloudflare solver.
- **A link to an arr taken out of the stack** goes at the next `apply`, with that arr's
  key. One renamed in Prowlarr stays, as it may be yours now, and drift reports it as
  still in the app. To keep a link, run `mediaplane keep prowlarr.application_sonarr`
  (or `_radarr`) before that `apply`: it keeps the link as yours, and stops the report.

## Changing it

- **In `stack.yaml`,** under `apps.prowlarr`, you can set `port`, `version`, `env` and
  `enabled: false`. A different `version` is an untested combination, and `plan` warns
  about it. See the [`stack.yaml` reference](../../docs/reference/stack-yaml.md). For
  example, less logging:

  ```yaml
  apps:
    prowlarr:
      env:
        PROWLARR__LOG__LEVEL: warn
  ```

- **Anything else** goes in `compose.override.yaml` in the Mediaplane home. Compose merges
  it over the generated file, and `plan` shows which containers it recreates. For
  example, a memory limit:

  ```yaml
  services:
    prowlarr:
      mem_limit: 512m
  ```

  Don't override the variables listed above: Mediaplane relies on them.

## Known issues

- **The indexer proxy needs the internet to be made.** Prowlarr tests a new proxy as it
  saves it: it has the solver fetch a page of Prowlarr's own service,
  `https://prowlarr.servarr.com/v1/ping`. Without the internet, `apply` fails with
  `Unable to connect to proxy: HTTP request failed: [502:BadGateway]`; the
  [runbook](../../docs/runbooks/wiring-failed.md) says what to do. Byparr needs the
  internet anyway: its health check loads a web page.
- **A link goes when its arr leaves the stack.** Remove Sonarr or Radarr from
  `stack.yaml`, and the next `apply` removes its link from Prowlarr, which holds the arr's
  key, once `plan` has said so (`- remove prowlarr.application_radarr`). One renamed in
  Prowlarr stays, as it may be yours now: `plan` and `drift` say so; delete it in
  Prowlarr's web UI (Settings, then Apps) if you don't want it.
- **The indexer proxy goes when the stack drops its Cloudflare solver.** With no Byparr
  and no FlareSolverr, the next `apply` removes the proxy from Prowlarr, so it no longer
  sends the challenged requests of indexers tagged `cloudflare` to a solver that is gone.
  The `cloudflare` tag stays, on your indexers too. To keep the proxy instead, run
  `mediaplane keep prowlarr.indexer_proxy` before that `apply`.
- **Set up before Slice 3a.** If Prowlarr first started before Mediaplane wrote its
  `config.xml`, the file has no API key: Prowlarr takes its key from its environment, and
  doesn't write it there. `plan` lists `prowlarr.apiKey` under
  `Keys to put back in their apps' own files`, and Prowlarr as `> restart`: `apply` stops
  Prowlarr, puts the key in its `config.xml`, keeping the rest, and starts it again. If
  Mediaplane can't write the file (`keys.restore`), the
  [rebuilding a host runbook](../../docs/runbooks/rebuilding-a-host.md) says what to do.
- **Its key after a lost `state/`** is read back from `config.xml`, before anything is
  generated, as the [rebuilding a host runbook](../../docs/runbooks/rebuilding-a-host.md)
  says. One Mediaplane can't read stops `plan` (`keys.unrecoverable`): a new key would
  lock it out of Prowlarr.
